# Appendix B: Configuration Parameter Dictionary {#appendix-config-dictionary}

All values below are read from `pipelines/ci_model/shared/config.py` as of this document's writing — see @sec-maintenance for who is allowed to change them. These are the candidate-pool eligibility parameters, not the model's fitted weights (those are in `03_training/outputs/simple_rule_baseline_weights.json`, @sec-methodology).

| Parameter | Default | Type | Description | Risk if too high | Risk if too low |
|:---|---:|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `V3_RECENT_WINDOW_DAYS` | 90 | days | How recently a competitor must have bid to count as "recently active" | Stale/inactive competitors stay eligible longer than they should | Genuinely active competitors get dropped from the pool too soon |
| `V3_WARMUP_HISTORY_DAYS` | 365 | days | Lookback window for a competitor's general history when the recent window has too little data | Pool includes competitors whose relevant history is too old to matter | Pool misses competitors with a real but slightly older track record |
| `V3_WARMUP_RECENT_DAYS` | 365 | days | Companion lookback used alongside `V3_WARMUP_HISTORY_DAYS` | Same as above | Same as above |
| `V3_FALLBACK_LOOKBACK_DAYS` | 730 | days | Widest lookback window, used only when the narrower windows don't produce enough candidates | Very old, likely-irrelevant bidders can enter the pool | The pool can come up too small for a project with sparse regional history |
| `V3_RECURRING_REGIONAL_MIN_BIDS` | 3 | bid count | Minimum prior bids for a competitor to count as a "recurring regional" bidder | Companies with a thin, possibly-coincidental history get treated as regulars | Genuinely recurring regional bidders get excluded on a technicality |
| `V3_FALLBACK_SCORE_THRESHOLD` | 1.5 | weighted score | Minimum combined signal score for a competitor to clear the pool via the fallback path | Pool grows to include weakly-relevant competitors | Pool can shrink to miss real competitors who only partially match |
| `V3_PRIORITY_WEIGHT` | 3.0 | weight | Score contribution from CSI's own "priority competitor" flag | CSI-flagged companies can dominate the pool even with weak project-fit | CSI's own known competitors could fail to clear the pool |
| `V3_HISTORICAL_WINNER_WEIGHT` | 2.0 | weight | Score contribution from having won a similar project before | Past winners get over-weighted relative to newer credible bidders | A company's past wins stop mattering enough to keep them in the pool |
| `V3_RECURRING_REGIONAL_WEIGHT` | 1.5 | weight | Score contribution from recurring-regional-bidder status | Regional regulars can crowd out a project's more specific matches | Regional regulars can be dropped in favor of a one-off closer match |

: Configuration parameter dictionary — candidate-pool eligibility. {#tbl-config-dictionary}

::: {.callout-note}
Two other configuration values sit outside this table because they define the model's evaluation boundary, not its eligibility rules: `TRAIN_END_DATE = "2025-01-01"` and `VALIDATION_END_DATE = "2025-05-01"` (both in the same `shared/config.py`). Changing either means re-training and re-evaluating the model, not just re-running it — treat as a developer-only, not an admin-only, change.
:::

\newpage

# Appendix C: Example Walkthrough {#appendix-example-walkthrough}

## Example 1: Model-Output Path

Take `MN_STEARNS_CO_MELROSE_2023-08-03` — the same project key used as the worked example in @sec-report-guide's exact command. It is a real, resolved project in the delivery dataset: a Mill & Overlay job in Stearns County, MN (2,425 mix tons, 4,732 base tons, 9,485 SY of milling), with 11 recorded bids and a low bid of $1,273,463.90 from C & L Excavating — the actual historical winner.

Running the report generator command from @sec-report-guide against this project key produces a Deep Dive block (@tbl-key-fields) for each selected competitor, including C & L Excavating and RL Larson Excavating — the two closest competitors in the actual outcome (bids $1,273,463.90 and $1,274,862.52, roughly 0.1% apart). Confirming the specific predicted probability and threat-level figures a given run produces requires actually running the command — see the data-integrity caveats in @sec-methodology before treating any single number as a permanent benchmark — but the review workflow in @sec-report-guide applies directly here: an estimator familiar with Stearns County paving work would sanity-check the top-ranked names against the fact that these two firms did, in reality, finish 1st and 2nd within roughly $1,400 of each other.

## Example 2: User-Input Path

Suppose, for the same project, a CSI estimator's own top-3 gut-check includes C & L Excavating. Entering that name through the User-Input Path (@sec-solution-architecture) does not re-score or re-rank it against the ML model — it enriches the name with the same historical statistics the Deep Dive block would show, computed directly from the delivery dataset:

- **Bid Rate / overall history**: 33 recorded bids, 8 wins (24.2% win rate) across the full dataset.
- **Experience — same project type**: 13 prior Mill & Overlay bids, 4 wins (30.8% win rate on this specific project type) — both well above the 3-bid "insufficient data" floor (@sec-output-files), so this stat is shown as a real percentage, not flagged as insufficient.
- **Experience — same county**: 15 prior bids in Stearns County specifically.

As @sec-limitations notes, this enrichment is where the User-Input Path stops — CSI's own pick is never automatically compared against what the ML model would have ranked for the same project. An estimator wanting that comparison today has to read both outputs side by side themselves.

\newpage

# Appendix D: Glossary {#appendix-glossary}

| Term | Definition |
|:---|:---|
| Winner Hit Rate@K | Share of projects (with a resolvable winner) where the actual winner appears in the top K ranked/predicted competitors |
| Candidate pool | The set of competitors considered for ranking on a given project — either pre-filtered or full-universe |
| Full-universe ranking | Ranking directly over the entire known competitor set, with no pre-filtering step |
| Rule-based benchmark | A hand-written, explainable scoring rule used as a comparison point against the ML model |
| Fuzzy-match confirmation | The manual review step required before a new or ambiguous competitor name is added as a new entity vs. matched to an existing one |
| Model-output path | The ML/rule-based pipeline that predicts competitors for a new project |
| User-input path | The separate pipeline where CSI manually enters its own top-3 predicted competitors |
| Plan Reader | The agent that converts an uploaded PDF plan set into structured, human-verified project facts — see @sec-solution-architecture |
| Competitor Intelligence | The agent that predicts likely competitors and generates reports — the subject of most of this document |
| Priority Competitor | A company CSI already tracks as a known, frequent competitor (registry `Top Competitors Tag`) |
| Discovery Competitor | A company the system found supporting bid history for, that is not on CSI's known-priority list |
| Threat Level | The HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW label a report assigns a competitor, always rule-derived from its bid-likelihood percentage — see @sec-output-files |
| Deep Dive | The per-competitor block in a generated report containing bid rate, recency, capacity, experience, and win-rate stats — see @tbl-key-fields |
| `scratch.bid_projects` / `scratch.bid_results` | The shared Postgres tables both Plan Reader (writes) and Competitor Intelligence (reads) use — see @sec-solution-architecture |
| `row_source = 'plan_reader'` | The tag identifying which database rows originated from a human-verified plan upload, as opposed to CSI's bulk historical data load |

: Glossary of key terms. {#tbl-glossary}
